title: Image Western Blots for Quantitative Immunoblotting Using Bio-Rad VersaDoc CCD Camera
author: Doug Campbell
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jwscpee

steps.title: Gather materials for PVDF imaging
steps.instruction: Collect the PVDF membrane with its block, tweezers, and clean transparencies; bring them into the VersaDoc room.

steps.title: Transfer PVDF to transparency
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, remove the PVDF membrane from the block and place it onto a transparency.

steps.title: Prepare ECL detection reagent
steps.instruction: Mix Luminol and peroxide in a 1:1 ratio to obtain 850 µL of ECL reagent per sheet of PVDF.

steps.title: Wet PVDF with ECL reagent
steps.instruction: Apply the 850 µL ECL reagent to the PVDF on the transparency, fully covering the area where bands will appear.

steps.title: Place transparency on wet plate
steps.instruction: Wet the VersaDoc top plate with water, then position the transparency containing the PVDF and detection reagent onto the plate.

steps.title: Power on VersaDoc system
steps.instruction: Turn on the Black Box on the benchtop (camera) and listen for a faint click; then turn on the VersaDoc unit and allow its self‑test (door lights will cycle/flash). Do NOT scratch the glass inside VersaDoc and avoid metal tools around plates.

steps.title: Launch Quantity One software
steps.instruction: Start the Quantity One program on the computer.

steps.title: Connect software to VersaDoc
steps.instruction: In Quantity One select File → Versadoc; the program will connect to the camera.

steps.title: Select chemic super sensitivity mode
steps.instruction: When the Select Application screen appears, press Select and choose “chemic super sensitivity” under Blotting.

steps.title: Enable saturation highlight
steps.instruction: Activate Highlight Saturation so over‑exposed pixels appear red (red pixels cannot be quantified).

steps.title: Focus camera and set aperture
steps.instruction: Use the red sticker on the far left for top‑plate focus (small western blot) and the second red sticker for bottom‑plate focus; set the camera aperture to 1.4 (largest opening).

steps.title: Preview image briefly
steps.instruction: Press the Preview button for 1 second to view the membrane.

steps.title: Set optimal exposure and capture
steps.instruction: Press the Optimal Exposure (stacking) button; set start exposure between 10–30 seconds and end exposure between 60–300 seconds (determine experimentally); click OK to begin imaging of up to 30 frames. Record the exposure times in your lab notebook.

steps.title: Resolve exposure errors if any
steps.instruction: If an error occurs, press OK, re‑select Optimal Exposure, re‑enter the exposure times, and continue.

steps.title: Select best images
steps.instruction: From the 30 captured frames, choose the 2–3 best photos, avoiding any with red saturated areas.

steps.title: Adjust image with gamma
steps.instruction: For a chosen image, select Image → Transform; in the Transform window apply the Gamma function to improve appearance.

steps.title: Save and back up images
steps.instruction: Save the adjusted image as both JPEG and SCN files; copy them to the C drive, M drive, and Dropbox using the naming format year.month.day.

steps.title: Print image for notebook
steps.instruction: Print a copy of the image; in the Print screen set page setup to 1280 × 1280 pixels.

steps.title: Remove transparency and clean plate
steps.instruction: Take the transparency out of the VersaDoc, discard excess liquid into the green bin, and wipe the wet plate with a Kimwipe.

steps.title: Return PVDF to storage
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, place the PVDF membrane back into its container with the block.

steps.title: Shut down equipment
steps.instruction: Turn off the VersaDoc, the Black Box camera, and the computer.
